dialogs.title: บทสนทนา — Viewing a room in a ซอย near the BTS
dialogs.intro: Budi is looking for a place to live. Pay attention to the rent figure — it uses *หมื่น*, a unit English doesn't have and the one newcomers most often mishear.

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [สวัสดี|Sà-wàt-dii][ครับ|khráp] [มี|Mii][ห้อง|hâwng][ว่าง|wâang][ไหม|mǎi][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: Good afternoon. Do you have a room available?

lines.speaker: เจ้าของ:
lines.text: [มี|Mii][ค่ะ|khâ] [ชั้น|Chán][สี่|sìi][ห้อง|hâwng][หนึ่ง|nùeng][ค่ะ|khâ] [ขึ้น|Khûen][ไป|pai][ดู|duu][ก่อน|kàwn][ไหม|mǎi][คะ|khá]
lines.id: Yes. One room on the fourth floor. Would you like to go up and see it first?
lines.literal: have — (polite). floor — four — room — one — (polite). go-up — go — see — first — (question) — (polite)?

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ครับ|Khráp] [ค่าเช่า|Khâa-châo][เดือน|duuean][ละ|lá][เท่าไหร่|thâo-rài][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: Yes. How much is the rent per month?

lines.speaker: เจ้าของ:
lines.text: [หนึ่ง|Nùeng][หมื่น|mùuen][สอง|sǎawng][พัน|phan][ค่ะ|khâ] [ยัง|Yang][ไม่|mâi][รวม|ruam][ค่าน้ำ|khâa-náam][ค่าไฟ|khâa-fai][ค่ะ|khâ]
lines.id: Twelve thousand. Water and electricity not included.
lines.literal: one — ten-thousand — two — thousand — (polite). still — not — include — water-fee — power-fee — (polite).

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ต้อง|Tâwng][วาง|waang][มัดจำ|mát-jam][ไหม|mǎi][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: Do I have to pay a deposit?

lines.speaker: เจ้าของ:
lines.text: [ต้อง|Tâwng][ค่ะ|khâ] [สอง|Sǎawng][เดือน|duuean][ค่ะ|khâ] [สัญญา|Sǎn-yaa][หนึ่ง|nùeng][ปี|pii][ค่ะ|khâ]
lines.id: Yes. Two months. The contract is one year.
lines.literal: must — (polite). two — month — (polite). contract — one — year — (polite).

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ห้อง|Hâwng][กว้าง|kwâang][ดี|dii][ครับ|khráp] [มี|Mii][แอร์|aae][ด้วย|dûai][ครับ|khráp] [เครื่องซักผ้า|Khrûeang-sák-phâa][มี|mii][ไหม|mǎi][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: The room's nice and spacious. There's AC too. Is there a washing machine?
lines.literal: room — spacious — good — (polite). have — AC — too — (polite). machine-wash-clothes — have — (question) — (polite)?

lines.speaker: เจ้าของ:
lines.text: [ในห้อง|Nai-hâwng][ไม่มี|mâi mii][ค่ะ|khâ] [อยู่|Yùu][ข้างล่าง|khâang-lâang][ค่ะ|khâ] [ข้างๆ|Khâang-khâang][ที่จอดรถ|thîi-jàwt-rót][ค่ะ|khâ]
lines.id: Not in the room. It's downstairs, next to the parking lot.
lines.literal: in-room — not-have — (polite). located — downstairs — (polite). beside — place-park-car — (polite).

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ใกล้|Klâi][บีทีเอส|BTS][ไหม|mǎi][ครับ|khráp]

lines.speaker: เจ้าของ:
lines.text: [เดิน|Dooen][ห้า|hâa][นาที|naa-thii][ค่ะ|khâ] [ตรง|Trong][ปาก|pàak][ซอย|sawy][มี|mii][ร้าน|ráan][สะดวกซื้อ|sà-dùak-súue][ด้วย|dûai][ค่ะ|khâ]
lines.id: Five minutes' walk. There's a convenience store at the mouth of the soi too.
lines.literal: walk — five — minute — (polite). right-at — mouth — soi — have — shop — convenient-buy — too — (polite).

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ดี|Dii][เลย|loei][ครับ|khráp] [ขอ|Khǎaw][คิด|khít][ดู|duu][ก่อน|kàwn][นะ|ná][ครับ|khráp] [เดี๋ยว|Dǐao][โทร|thoo][มา|maa][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: Great. Let me think about it first. I'll call you.
lines.literal: good — really — (polite). ask — think — see — first — okay — (polite). in-a-moment — phone — come — (polite).

notes: **ค่า khâa means "fee, cost", and it attaches to the front of anything you pay for.** *ค่าเช่า* (rent), *ค่าน้ำ* (water bill), *ค่าไฟ* (electricity), *ค่าอาหาร* (food costs), *ค่ารถ* (fare), *ค่าเทอม khâa-thoome* (school fees). This one pattern saves you dozens of words.

⚠️ **หนึ่งหมื่นสองพัน = 12,000, not 1,200.** *หมื่น mùuen* is ten thousand, a unit with no single-word equivalent in English — and it's the number one reason newcomers mishear rent prices. If in doubt, ask for it in writing: *เขียนให้หน่อยได้ไหมครับ*.

**ซอย sawy is a lane or side street branching off a main road**, and every Bangkok address is built on it: *สุขุมวิท ซอย 11* means lane number 11 off Sukhumvit Road. *ปากซอย pàak sawy* (mouth of the soi) is where the lane meets the main road — and it's the landmark everyone uses to meet up.
**ข้างล่าง khâang-lâang (below) and ข้างบน khâang-bon (above) are used for building floors** too, not just for where things are. *อยู่ข้างล่าง* = it's downstairs.
**ข้างๆ khâang-khâang means "next to"** — with repetition. Without repetition, *ข้าง* alone more often becomes part of another word (*ข้างใน, ข้างนอก*).

**มัดจำ mát-jam is a security deposit.** In Bangkok, two months' rent is the usual amount, and by custom (not law) it's returned when you move out if there's no damage. Ask for a written *สัญญา sǎn-yaa* (contract), and keep photos of the room's condition on day one.

**ขอคิดดูก่อนนะครับ/คะ is the key phrase you already met in unit 12.** Here it's used honestly — to really think it over. But remember, the same sentence often means a gentle no when a Thai person says it to you.
**โทร thoo is short for โทรศัพท์ thoo-rá-sàp** and means "to phone". *เดี๋ยวโทรมา* (I'll call you), *โทรหา thoo hǎa* (to call someone).

after: Notice **ตู้ tûu** (cabinet/box), which forms many words: *ตู้เย็น* (cold cabinet = fridge), *ตู้เสื้อผ้า* (clothes cabinet = wardrobe), *ตู้เอทีเอ็ม* (ATM), *ตู้ไปรษณีย์* (mailbox). It's the same pattern as *โรง-*, *นัก-*, *ค่า-*, and *น้ำ-* that you've already met.

blocks.title: Reporting a problem
items: **…เสีย *sǐa*** — broken. *แอร์เสียครับ* (the AC is broken), *น้ำไม่ไหลครับ náam mâi lǎi* (the water isn't running), *ไฟดับ fai dàp* (the power's out).
**ช่วยมาดูหน่อยได้ไหมครับ/คะ** — could you come and take a look?
**ซ่อมได้เมื่อไหร่ครับ/คะ *sâwm dâai mûea-rài*** — when can it be fixed?
⚠️ The word *เสีย sǐa* has several meanings: broken, lost, and also "to pay" (*เสียค่าเช่า*). Which one is meant is always clear from the sentence.

blocks.text: Thai adjectives come **after** the noun and need no "is": *ห้องกว้าง* (the room is spacious), *ห้องไม่สะอาด* (the room isn't clean). To intensify, add *มาก mâak* (very) or *จัง jang* (so) after: *กว้างมาก*, *สะอาดจัง*.

blocks.title: One thing to check in Bangkok
items: **Ask about the electricity rate per unit.** Many rental buildings set their own rate, well above the state rate, and with the AC on every night the difference can be bigger than a rent increase. The phrase: *ค่าไฟยูนิตละเท่าไหร่ครับ/คะ khâa-fai yuu-nít lá thâo-rài*.

**Check the real walking distance to the station.** "Five minutes" in an ad often means five minutes by motorbike taxi. In Thai listings the honest word is *เดิน dooen* (walk) — if it isn't mentioned, it's most likely not on foot.
